title: Reported Speech: Pronoun Rules — Quiz 125A
content:
## Reported Speech: Pronoun Rules

Review the first, second and third person rules for reported speech.

### Lesson focus

1. Pronouns of the first person change according to the subject of the reporting verb.
2. Pronouns of the second person change according to the object of the reporting verb.
3. Pronouns of the third person normally do not change.

### Understand the pattern

First-person forms refer to the original speaker; second-person forms refer to the original listener. Track the people before choosing I, we, you, he, she or they. Third-person forms may stay the same, unless a change is needed to avoid ambiguity.

### Worked answers and explanation

Asha said to me, 'I can help you' → Asha told me that she could help me. I refers to Asha, while you refers to the reporter. The speaker's name alone does not tell you who every you in a quotation refers to.

### Try another

Report: I said to Rohan, 'You can use my book.'

### Suggested answer

I told Rohan that he could use my book. You becomes he because Rohan is the listener; my stays my because the reporter owns the book.
